sources.title: Learning When to Remember: Risk-Sensitive Contextual Bandits for Abstention-Aware Memory Retrieval in LLM-Based Coding Agents
sources.artifact_note: paper states code and deterministic local artifacts are available at the repository listed in the paper; repository identity was not independently bound in this run

sources.title: MedExpMem: Adapting Experience Memory for Differential Diagnosis

observations.text: RSCB-MC makes no_memory and abstain first-class memory-controller actions and explicitly separates retrieval evidence from permission to inject memory. On 32 hard negatives, static hybrid retrieval has 75.0% false-positive memory injection and 100.0% unsafe injection, while full RSCB-MC reports 0.0% false positives and 100.0% correct safe non-injection.

RSCB-MC provides direct outcome-bearing ablation evidence for abstention: in deterministic offline replay, full RSCB-MC reports 0.0% false positives and cumulative reward -31.740; removing abstention/non-injection actions raises false positives to 17.5% and worsens cumulative reward to -87.800. The paper explicitly calls removal of abstention its strongest ablation.

RSCB-MC's main offline replay reports 62.5% non-oracle success with 0.0% false positives versus static retrieval at 50.0% success and 17.5% false positives. In the 200-case bounded hot-path proxy validation it reports 60.5% success with 0.0% false positives. These are deterministic/proxy coding-agent artifacts, not autonomous-science outcomes.

MedExpMem performs anatomical scoping, similarity-threshold retrieval, and an LLM relevance pass that excludes clearly irrelevant notes while retaining potentially useful ones. Despite those retrieval-side filters, reported harmful correct-to-incorrect memory effects remain nonzero across all seven model settings, ranging from 1.3% to 5.8%.

MedExpMem's Qwen3-VL-8B ablation supports retrieval selectivity but not receiver-side admission: the full threshold tau=0.90 configuration reaches 74.5% accuracy, versus 73.1% at tau=0.80 and 72.8% at tau=0.95. The agent still autonomously uses retained notes after relevance scoring, so this does not isolate a post-retrieval accept/reject predicate.

protocol_inferences.name: EMPTY_MEMORY_IS_A_VALID_RUNTIME_ACTION
protocol_inferences.text: A memory controller must represent no-memory/abstain as valid operational outcomes rather than treating them as retrieval failure. Outcome-bearing RSCB-MC ablation evidence now independently supports the practical safety role of non-injection.

protocol_inferences.name: RETRIEVAL_FILTERING_DOES_NOT_DISCHARGE_ADMISSION_RISK
protocol_inferences.text: Domain/scoping, similarity thresholding, and relevance filtering can reduce candidate mismatch but do not prove that every retained memory is safe to influence the current action; MedExpMem's nonzero harmful-memory rates are clinical outcome evidence for this residual risk.

protocol_inferences.name: CANONICAL_ABSTENTION_INVARIANT_PROMOTION_JUSTIFIED_WITH_SCOPE
protocol_inferences.text: The combination of pre-submission clinical GSEM no-fill design, clinical MedExpMem residual harmful-memory outcomes, and direct coding-domain RSCB-MC abstention ablation justifies promoting abstention preservation to a generic runtime safety invariant. It does not establish that the invariant improves autonomous-science benchmark accuracy.

phase1_acceptance.reason: These sources support a runtime memory-admission invariant but depend on model/tool execution and do not provide an end-to-end zero-dependency scheduled-Chat parity route.

scope_notes: RSCB-MC outcome claims are limited to its deterministic coding-agent replay/proxy artifacts; do not generalize the reported gains to scientific agents.
MedExpMem harmful-memory rates establish residual risk after retrieval-side filtering, not the efficacy of a post-retrieval abstention gate.
Generic protocol promotion is a safety/lifecycle invariant supported by triangulation, not a claim of science-domain benchmark improvement.
